# Conditional native engine fixtures

These small projects exercise actual engine-owned lifecycle and state behavior. They are copied into a temporary directory beneath `tests/` before execution. The runner never installs engines, packages, export templates, platform modules, SDKs or licenses. Run `tests/test-native-engine-fixtures.sh`, or invoke its `.cjs` entrypoint with Node.

The runner always checks fixture structure and its process/report handling using explicitly labeled Node process simulations. It then reports separate native verdicts for each engine and the Unreal/Unity feature cases. Missing prerequisites produce `blocked`; intentionally unselected builds or exports produce `not-run`. Structural success does not establish native acceptance. `--structure-only` skips native launches; `--require-native` requires all three native smoke verdicts, all twelve Unreal feature cases and all fifteen automated Unity feature cases to pass. Manual/service/player/visual/device acceptance remains separately scoped. A default run may exit successfully with blocked prerequisites; inspect the individual verdicts and JSON summary.

| Selection | Required configuration | Optional production check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unity | `HEPHAERA_UNITY_EDITOR` or Unity on PATH, plus exact `HEPHAERA_UNITY_VERSION` matching the installed Editor | Set `HEPHAERA_UNITY_BUILD_TARGET` to `StandaloneWindows64`, `StandaloneLinux64` or `StandaloneOSX`. A matching installed platform module is required. |
| Godot | `HEPHAERA_GODOT_EDITOR` or Godot on PATH; the fixture uses Godot 4 GDScript | Set `HEPHAERA_GODOT_EXPORT_PRESET` to `Linux`, `Windows` or `macOS`; matching installed export templates are required. |
| Unreal | `HEPHAERA_UNREAL_EDITOR` or UnrealEditor on PATH, `HEPHAERA_UNREAL_UBT` or UnrealBuildTool on PATH, `HEPHAERA_UNREAL_VERSION`, and `HEPHAERA_UNREAL_PROJECT=tests/fixtures/engines/unreal/HephaeraNativeFixture.uproject` | Compilation and the selected Automation test are required together. No binary map or content asset is fabricated. |

Executable selections accept a single executable path or PATH name, without embedded arguments. Unreal Build Tool may also be an explicitly selected `.dll`, run by an installed `dotnet`. Unreal project selection is confined to this fixture's repository-local `unreal/` directory; arbitrary project injection is rejected. The supplied source project uses a transient world and components, so it requires no checked-in binary assets.

`HEPHAERA_NATIVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` controls each native invocation, from 1 through 600 seconds (default 180). Timed-out and cancelled runs terminate their owned process trees. Native results are validated against engine-produced reports and expected checks, not merely exit code zero. Temporary logs and outputs are removed after results are summarized; use the task's captured runner output for durable availability evidence. No visual, listening, accessibility or physical haptic acceptance is claimed by these fixtures.

Unity disables Package Manager for the base fixture's builtin-only dependencies. Its Editor smoke checks ScriptableObject serialization and lifecycle; the optional build records a real BuildReport and runs a matching host player. Godot checks node enter/ready/exit state and explicit failure exits; an optional host export is launched independently. Unreal compiles the explicitly selected fixture, executes only `Hephaera.Fixtures.LifecycleState`, and checks the real Automation report. Signing, publishing and running another project's tests remain outside this fixture.

The separate [Unity feature fixture](unity/features/README.md) contains sixteen native case methods, of which fifteen are eligible for automated execution, and ten supplemental procedures. Select a prepared offline configuration through `HEPHAERA_UNITY_FEATURE_CONFIG`. Exact package selections must match its manifest/lock and already installed project-local caches; ordinary runs use `-noUpm` and never restore dependencies. The package-inventory case remains a prepared-Editor-only procedure because its API is unavailable with UPM disabled. Native assets, graphics, WebGL platform modules and usable audio output are conditional prerequisites. Play Mode runs change reload options only in the copied fixture process and do not certify a host project's reload behavior. Optional CLI/Pipeline and online service verification require their separately configured and authorized environments. See the fixture instructions for report identities, preparation and claim limits.

The separate [Unreal feature fixture](unreal/features/README.md) exercises twelve native families. Select it explicitly with `HEPHAERA_UNREAL_FEATURE_PROJECT=tests/fixtures/engines/unreal/features/HephaeraFeatureFixture.uproject`. It targets UE 5.8 as a test baseline and does not set host-project policy. Its isolated Editor project explicitly selects GAS, Game Features, Niagara and PCG plugins and links the MassEntity runtime module. Missing native assets block only their dependent cases; source-only cases still require the actual compiler and Editor. Each invocation uses a fresh report directory and nonce recorded by the real Automation test; empty discovery, error events, failed processes, incomplete and stale reports cannot establish success. See the feature instructions for remaining multiplayer, packaged, visual and device acceptance limits.
